neighbours.label: scalar-emphasis follow-up: the word right after a frame that marks what follows as a surprising extreme ('And that's with …', 'and this is from a man who …', 'even for …', 'and that's just …', 'hard enough for … to')
fire: The company lost two million dollars last quarter. And that's with record sales in December.
He called the film unwatchable, and this is from a critic who praises almost everything.
The exam was brutal even for students who had studied all year.
The repairs will cost nine thousand pounds, and that's just for the roof.
It is difficult enough for a native speaker to read his handwriting.
She finished the marathon in under three hours. And that's with a sprained ankle.
The climb is dangerous even for guides who know the mountain well.
Grandpa said the chili was too spicy, and this is from someone who eats raw peppers.
quiet: The company lost two million dollars last quarter despite record sales in December.
He reviewed the film alongside a critic who praises almost everything.
The exam was scheduled for students who had studied all year.
The repairs will cost nine thousand pounds, mostly for the roof.
It is a pleasure for a native speaker to read his handwriting.
She finished the marathon in under three hours after resting a sprained ankle.
The climb is led by guides who know the mountain well.
Grandpa shared the chili with someone who eats raw peppers.

notes: Card: peak tokens ',' x5, ' even' x3, ' with' x2, ' for' x2, ' just' x2. Probes: "And that's with their best player" 1.03, 'even for experienced hikers' 0.89, 'and this is from a man who' 0.80, "and that's just for starters" 0.58, 'hard enough for adults to' 0.47; the same content without the emphasis frame 0.01-0.23; "I'm not even sure" 0.18. The + pole is flagged dense (25.6%); this test is of the - pole only.
